roleTitle: Machine Learning Engineer, Retail Store Operations
jobDescription: Store operations at a regional grocery chain use a shelf-gap detection model on camera images to trigger restocking tasks. The Machine Learning Engineer owns the detection model end-to-end, decides when a new version is released to stores, runs the model's production monitoring, and is the accountable owner of its performance towards the store operations director.
requirements: Owns the shelf-gap detection model end-to-end and decides when new versions are released to stores.
Builds and maintains the training, labelling and evaluation pipelines for the model.
Monitors the model in production across stores and runs the monthly model review.
Coordinates releases with store operations and the platform team and records own responsibility boundaries.
Documents model cards, known limitations and hand-over conditions for each version.

evidence.text: Built and maintained the labelling and training pipelines for the shelf-gap detection model, including the active-learning loop that queues low-confidence images for the labelling team.
Ran the offline evaluation for each candidate version on the held-out store images and wrote up the results for the computer vision lead, who decided which version went to the pilot stores.
Maintained the production monitoring dashboards for the pilot stores and prepared the monthly review pack; the computer vision lead presented it to store operations.
Wrote the model card sections on training data and limitations for versions 1.3 to 1.5, including the limitation that promotional end-cap displays were under-represented in training images.

Responsibilities included pipeline development, offline evaluation, monitoring dashboards and model-card documentation for the detection model over about eighteen months, reporting to the computer vision lead.
Work sample: the active-learning pipeline configuration and the model card for version 1.5, with the training job identifiers as a verification trail.
Reference call with the former computer vision lead: said the candidate was 'the one keeping the whole model running day to day' and that 'in practice it was his model'; confirmed employment dates.
Hiring manager pre-read: the store operations director wants an engineer who has personally decided model releases to live stores; please separate what the candidate decided from what he prepared.
